🚢 SHIPBUILDING ANCILLARY SERIES 

Company # — Rappid Valves (India) Ltd | NSE: RAPPID 299

India’s shipbuilding story isn’t only about shipyards.

The bigger opportunity may sit with critical ancillaries supplying every vessel.

🔹 Rappid manufactures industrial & marine valves
🔹 Supplies into naval, shipbuilding & repair applications
🔹 Approved/registered with multiple Indian shipyards
🔹 ClassNK marine certification adds credibility
🔹 Moving beyond valves → valve + actuator + control-panel integration

🔥 Naval trigger

Recent orders linked to the Indian Navy Fleet Support Ship programme:

BHEL — ₹18.06 Cr
Shree Refrigerations — ₹8.55 Cr
Müller-BBM — ₹3.25 Cr

Total: ~₹29.85 Cr

Plus L&T — ₹2.84 Cr FSS-related order.

Executable order book: ~₹40 Cr, versus FY26 revenue of ~₹53 Cr.

📈 FY26

Revenue: ₹53.2 Cr
EBITDA: ₹10.3 Cr
PAT: ₹6.5 Cr

But there is a major red flag:

CFO: –₹10.8 Cr
Debtor days: ~170
Inventory days: ~258

So the thesis is NOT simply “order book = multibagger.”

I want to see:

Revenue growth + margin stability + positive cash flow + improving working capital.

If those start appearing together, Rappid could become an interesting small-cap naval shipbuilding ancillary to watch.

Series lesson:

> In India’s shipbuilding boom, don't just track who builds the ship. Track who supplies the critical components inside it. 🚢⚙️

Fineotex Chemical — ₹800 Cr fund raise. Something big  brewing? 👀

Fineotex has sought approval to raise up to ₹800 Cr through equity/equity-linked instruments, with inorganic growth explicitly among the stated uses.

The interesting part: FCL is already cash-rich and debt-free.
So why potentially raise ₹800 Cr?
Its recent acquisition track record gives a clue.
In Dec-25, FCL acquired a 53.33% controlling stake in the US-based CrudeChem Technologies Group for ~$11.5m (~₹96 Cr).
CrudeChem had ~$68m revenue, strong US oilfield-chemicals customers and R&D/manufacturing infrastructure in Texas.
And this acquisition has been firing on all cylinders.
Capacity has already expanded from ~80K MTPA to ~140K MTPA, with strong demand, customer additions and wallet-share gains. ICRA recently highlighted the acquisition as a key driver of Fineotex's scale and diversification.

Management had also said it plans to gradually increase its ownership in CrudeChem to 80% in next 2 years. But even taking the CrudeChem stake higher wouldn't come close to explaining a potential ₹800 Cr raise.

That raises the obvious question:
Is Fineotex preparing for a really large acquisition?

Nothing has been announced yet.
But given the stock price action, market might be expecting something BIG.
₹800 Cr war chest + proven acquisition execution => something interesting to track !!

🇺🇸 FED CHAIR WARSH TURNS HAWKISH; PUTS INFLATION BACK AT CENTER

📌 Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said price stability remains the Fed’s top priority.

📉 Summer inflation data improved, but Warsh said underlying inflation trends have not changed materially.

🎯 Reaffirmed the 2% PCE inflation target as “firm and fixed.”

⚠️ Fed needs confidence inflation is returning to target; otherwise, more policy work may be required.

💪 US economy remains resilient — consumer spending healthy, labour market stable and business investment rising strongly.

💳 Warsh said financial conditions do not appear particularly restrictive, with credit markets showing limited signs of policy restraint.

🏦 At the July Fed meeting, a “good majority” preferred waiting before changing interest rates.

🔴 Impact: Hawkish / Negative for rate-sensitive assets — comments reduce expectations of aggressive Fed easing and may support bond yields and the US dollar.

Underappreciated SBI MF's distribution moat 

SBI MF's biggest advantage isn't fund performance. It's distribution. In India, bank-backed AMCs blessed with an edge as the bank branch is still the most powerful financial distribution channel
Investors trust banks with savings, salaries & FDs. Convincing a depositor to buy a bank-sponsored MF is far easier than acquiring a customer from scratch. Trust compounds over time
This trust factor is visible across the industry. 4 of India's top 5 AMCs are bank-backed. Even with rising competition, large AMCs have largely retained market share
SBI has the widest reach across the country, with one of the largest branch networks, customer bases & geographic presence among all financial institutions. That reach is difficult to replicate
Unlike most AMCs, SBI MF gets disproportionate support from its parent. SBI Bank contributes 35% of SBI MF's equity AUM. Compare that with just 8% for ICICI AMC & 6% for HDFC AMC
More interestingly, 40% of SBI MF's equity AUM comes through bank channels, versus 19% for ICICI AMC & 12% for HDFC AMC. SBI's distribution engine remains a major growth driver
Most banks operate open architecture & recommend products across AMCs based on suitability. SBI may have open architecture formally, but data suggests SBI customers get mostly SBI-branded investment products
The numbers are striking. 100% of SBI MF's promoter-bank sourced AUM sits with SBI, vs 70% for ICICI AMC & just 28% for HDFC AMC. That's about as captive as distribution gets
SBI's MF penetration opportunity is still huge. Average MF AUM per SBI branch is only ~10% of retail deposits per branch, implying a long runway for existing customers to migrate from deposits into MFs
The next leg of growth likely comes from B30 markets. SBI MF already has the highest B30 equity AUM share at 16%, ahead of ICICI AMC (12%) & HDFC AMC (11%)
SBI's deep Tier-2/Tier-3 presence matters. 66% of SBI MF's SIPs originate from B30 markets, giving it access to underpenetrated investors who are just beginning their financialization journey
The final edge is economics. SBI MF's distribution cost through SBI is just 65 bps, lower than HDFC AMC's 68 bps & ICICI AMC's 69 bps. Better reach + higher trust + lower cost = a distribution moat that's hard to disrupt

India's Lithium Battery Costs 23% Above China — Import Premium Adding $7-12 Per kWh as Grid-Scale Storage Deployment Accelerates

The Price Gap
India's landed LFP (Lithium Iron Phosphate) battery cell prices were 13–23% higher than China's after-tax prices in July

Landed LFP cell prices in India: $62–67 per kWh (~₹5,944–6,423 per kWh)

China's prices: ~$54.5 per kWh (~₹5,209 per kWh)

Additional cost for Indian buyers: $7–12 per kWh (~₹671–1,150 per kWh)

Similar price differential seen for assembled AC containers

Per report by JMK Research & Analytics and IEEFA

Why the Gap Exists
Attributed to freight, duties and other import-related costs

Local cell and pack manufacturing would help developers "avoid this import surcharge and reduce reliance on Chinese supply"

China Prices — Falling
Average prices of 314Ah LFP cells (widely used in utility-scale BESS) fell 1.4% month-on-month in July to CNY0.370 per Wh (~$54.5 per kWh)

Aided by 10.7% month-on-month fall in lithium carbonate prices

Additional supply from restart of CATL's Jianxiawo mine

Ample availability of 314Ah cells and stronger bargaining power among buyers

AC Container Prices — Sticky
Prices of integrated two-hour liquid-cooled AC containers remained unchanged at $85.7 per kWh (~₹8,216 per kWh)

~$30 per kWh difference between LFP cell and assembled container reflects additional equipment and services for grid-scale deployment:
Power conversion systems
Thermal management
Fire safety
Energy management systems
Commissioning and warranties

India's Storage Deployment — Accelerating
Commissioned ~8,236 MWh of BESS capacity during April–July FY27

Alongside 250 MW of pumped hydro storage

July alone: ~710 MWh of ESS capacity commissioned

Domestic downstream capacity: 6.35 GWh in July — led by Waaree ESS (5.15 GWh through container plant) and Midwest Energy (1.2 GWh integration facility)

Commercial Cell Manufacturing — Still Limited
Commercial cell manufacturing in India "remains limited"

Leaving BESS industry substantially dependent on imported cells

Government's ACC Tender
Ministry of Heavy Industries tendered remaining 10 GWh under 50-GWh ACC battery production-linked incentive scheme — exclusively for grid-scale storage

Requires domestic value addition of 25% within two years and 40% within five years

Core Theme
India's 13–23% battery cost premium over China is a structural competitiveness gap in its grid-scale storage ambitions — with commercial cell manufacturing still nascent and import dependence high, the ACC PLI scheme's localisation mandates are the critical policy lever to close the cost gap as India's BESS deployment accelerates rapidly.

⚡ Tata Power has been specifically cited as one of the listed companies whose shares could potentially be used in the swap.

💰 Other options reportedly include a direct Tata Sons buyout of SP Group’s stake financed by overseas banks, or sale of the stake to an external investor.

🟢 Impact: Positive for Tata Power, Tata Investment & Tata Chemicals sentiment — any resolution of SP Group’s 18.4% Tata Sons stake could revive hopes of Tata Sons value unlocking and reduce the long-running ownership overhang.

https://x.com/RaviBhandari83

The Relationship Trump Misunderstood:
For three decades, China and emerging markets effectively exported disinflation to the developed world. They produced goods at a fraction of Western costs and shipped them to consumers in the US and Europe. The result: lower prices and higher purchasing power
The West got cheaper TVs, phones, clothes, furniture and industrial goods. China got manufacturing jobs, export growth and rising incomes. It wasn't a one-way relationship. Both sides benefited
As exports surged, China accumulated enormous foreign exchange reserves. Every dollar earned from exports added to a growing pool of savings that had to be invested somewhere
Those reserves served two purposes: protect the yuan from volatility and build strategic national wealth. China used them to buy foreign assets, resources, companies and financial securities around the world
A large portion of those reserves found their way into US Treasuries. China became one of the largest lenders to the US government, recycling export earnings back into America's financial system
This mattered because sustained Treasury demand helped keep long-term US interest rates lower than they otherwise would have been. Cheap imports lowered inflation. Treasury purchases lowered financing costs
In effect, China was helping on two fronts: suppressing goods inflation through low-cost manufacturing and supporting bond markets through reserve recycling. 
Trump focused heavily on one side of the equation: the trade deficit. From that perspective, China was exporting too much and manufacturing jobs were leaving America. This became the basis for tariffs and trade confrontation.
But the other side received less attention. Those same imports were keeping prices low for US consumers. Many products became affordable precisely because they were manufactured in lower-cost economies
The relationship also extended to capital markets. China's reserve accumulation created a steady source of demand for US government bonds, helping support the broader financial system
Today that world is changing. China is no longer a low-income economy desperate for export growth. Wages have risen, technology has improved and its economic influence is far greater than it was 20 years ago
The old model of unlimited cheap labour, ever-rising globalization and automatic reserve recycling is fading. Both countries increasingly view the relationship through a strategic lens rather than purely an economic one
As supply chains fragment and tariffs rise, the US may face more inflation from its own policy choices. Producing goods domestically or through alternative supply chains is often more resilient, but rarely cheaper
At the same time, if foreign demand for Treasuries becomes less predictable, bond investors may demand higher yields to absorb increasing government debt. Higher yields mean higher financing costs across the economy
The next decade may look very different from the last three. Less globalization, more strategic competition, potentially higher inflation and structurally higher interest rates. Markets are still figuring out what that world looks like
Bottom line: The US-China relationship wasn't simply buyer vs seller. It was a system where goods, capital and inflation dynamics were deeply intertwined. Breaking that system may create consequences on both sides.

MORGAN STANLEY ON ON CYIENT

Maintains an Underweight rating; target price: ₹820.

The broader industry transformation from a capacity-led to a value-led outcomes model is steadily gaining traction.

Management is actively shifting toward annuity-based contracts, with project-based revenue currently accounting for 25% to 35% of the total.

Cyient Semiconductors targets a 4x scale in revenue alongside gross margins above 40% and EBIT margins exceeding 20% by F31.

These strategic initiatives favorably but is not yet baking in any material near-term business changes.

Execution remains the key catalyst before the firm turns constructive on the stock.

BERNSTEIN ON INDIA BANKS

Loan growth gap between private and public banks has narrowed to 1 percentage point from a peak of 4 percentage points.

Private banks are gaining loan and deposit market share amid positive deposit growth momentum.

Public banks are achieving superior net interest income growth, running about 4 percentage points ahead due to stronger spread performance.

A robust retail mix is supporting margin resilience and sustaining the profitability lead for public banks.

Asset quality remains benign across the sector, backed by low credit costs and healthy slippage trends.

The upcoming ECL transition poses a key medium-term risk for public banks regarding capital and8 credit costs.

CYIENT: ANALYST MEET HIGHLIGHTS

📈 TAM expanded from $100 bn to $2.4–3.2 tn through full lifecycle engineering.

💼 DET EBIT margin improved to 13.2% in Q1FY27 from 12.2% in FY26.

🎯 Targets around 15% EBIT margin by FY28 through AI and cost optimisation.

🚀 FY27 focused on transformation, FY28 on scaling and growth.

📌 FY31 target: industry-leading growth with 16% EBIT margin.

🔹 Cyient Semiconductors targets ~4x revenue and >20% EBIT margin by FY31.

HINDUSTAN COPPER OFS: ANALYSTS CAUTIOUS

🏛️ Government OFS includes 3% base offer + 3% greenshoe, potentially taking stake sale to 6%.

💰 OFS offered at nearly 10% discount.

⚠️ Analysts remain cautious on retail participation due to elevated valuations after the recent rally in metal stocks.

📌 Analysts see limited near-term upside and suggest waiting for better entry opportunities.

JPM on Dixon Tech
OW, TP Rs 16400

Government launched Mobile phone manufacturing scheme (MPMS) with an outlay of Rs625bn

How can it play out for Dixon:
1) There is an eligibility criteria of Rs100bn turnover in FY26 for mobile phone manufacturers, including EMS companies, meaning the benefit may not apply to all of Dixon’s customers, thereby limiting benefits only to top customers.
2) There is a sales threshold of Rs50bn required over FY26 sales to avail incentives, meaning the scheme seems to be focused more on exports given domestic mobile shipments seem to have hit a ceiling for the industry; hence, for Dixon to avail benefits it will have to ramp up exports.
3) There is a 1.5% additional incentive on local sourcing of components and sub-assemblies, where Dixon should be eligible to get incentives of 0.6% given it is scaling up manufacturing of camera modules and display modules.

While all these factors should lead to earnings upgrades, quantum of that is still unclear as it will be dependent on
1) export volumes Dixon can achieve over the scheme period,
2) negotiations with brands on incentive sharing.

Acquisition is inexpensive and could be EPS neutral or accretive.

TCS may increasingly use M&A to fill capability gaps and enter new growth areas.

CITI ON TCS — SELL | TP ₹1,825

Citi says the acquisition will anchor a long-term strategic partnership with Porsche.

Assuming €600–700 million FY28 revenue run-rate and 7–9% EBIT margins, the deal implies roughly 5–8x EV/EBIT.

Valuations appear low, but Citi flags revenue-decline risk, noting European IT peers trade at similar valuations.

Such acquisitions could support near-term growth, but the risk of the existing business declining YoY is increasing.

Citi remains cautious on the Indian IT sector.

JEFFERIES ON CONSUMER FINANCE — POSITIVE

Jefferies says NBFCs’ YTD stock returns have been earnings-driven, not valuation-driven.

NBFCs have outperformed banks, largely led by EPS and book-value upgrades.

P/B multiples for most players, including Bajaj Finance, Chola Finance and Shriram Finance, are down YTD despite strong growth.

Porsche engagement provides a long-term strategic relationship.

Sees the acquisition as complementary to TCS, but expects the financial impact to remain limited.

Deal could add ~3% to revenue growth and <1% to PAT, assuming mid-single-digit margins.

Morgan Stanley sees TCS increasingly using the M&A route to fill capability gaps and white spaces.

CITI ON OIL & GAS

India’s energy-security policy is expanding beyond emergency response into a broader long-term strategy.

Government’s agenda spans strategic petroleum reserves (SPRs), import substitution, higher domestic production, gas adoption and upstream exploration.

ONGC could directly shoulder incremental capital deployment toward SPRs and offshore exploration & production.

GAIL could participate in coal gasification, fertiliser JVs and LPG pipeline projects.

Potential government compensation remains a key monitorable for Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs).

Citi prefers OMCs and GAIL.

BERNSTEIN ON PB FINTECH — OUTPERFORM | TP ₹2,310

Bernstein says PB Fintech has built a strong sales engine with high growth, high renewals and lower claims.

Higher operating performance is translating into strong take-rates.

PB Fintech is delivering 30–35%+ topline growth at scale, despite slower industry growth.

Near-term regulatory risks remain, but channel checks suggest any pricing/take-rate cuts are unlikely to be harsh.

Bernstein believes regulatory delays partly reflect recognition that higher take-rates have underlying justification, while industry growth remains a regulatory priority.

JEFFERIES ON HOSPITAL SECTOR

Jefferies says MPD-2047 aims to strengthen Delhi’s position as a healthcare and medical-tourism hub.

Plan focuses on expanded infrastructure, better local & regional connectivity and policies supporting higher-density development.

Removal of height restrictions and higher FAR could improve land utilisation and enable hospital capacity additions.

Direct benefits are expected to be strongest for hospital assets in Delhi.

Max Healthcare, Fortis Healthcare and Medanta could be key beneficiaries due to their strong NCR presence.

JEFFERIES ON UPL — ACCUMULATE | TP ₹715

Jefferies met UPL’s senior management; company remains confident of achieving 10–14% full-year growth guidance.

Q2 growth is shaping up broadly in line with expectations.

EBITDA margins are expected to improve as UPL rationalises unprofitable parts of the business.

UPL is maintaining tight control over inventories in Latin America amid El Niño risks.

Marketing for the Advanta IPO is expected to begin soon.

NOMURA ON INDIAN HOTELS — ACCUMULATE | TP ₹830

Nomura expects the Oriental Hotels acquisition to be EPS accretive for Indian Hotels.

Further cost synergies could provide additional earnings benefits.

Asset optimisation and property upgrades could drive EBITDA higher.

The merger will also simplify the group’s holding structure.

HSBC ON INDIA STRATEGY — NEUTRAL

HSBC says Indian corporate earnings remain resilient for now despite the oil shock.

Results have come in ahead of expectations, with small & mid-cap earnings growth standing out.

GST cuts and RBI easing supported demand, while price hikes and inventory gains helped offset higher raw-material costs.

HSBC sees FY27 earnings growth at 14.3%, but expects some of the current support to fade in H2.

Maintains a Neutral stance on India within Asia.

Elevated commodity prices pose a risk of earnings downgrades in coming quarters.
